label: D1 after an a1->S1 common transition, early-to-mid episode
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO or D2), when the previous trial was a1 with a common transition to S1. The previous reward does not gate it: it fires after both rewarded and unrewarded trials. Firing gets rarer over the episode: rate about 12% of steps at trials 0-30, falling to near zero by trial ~70, and it is silent from trial 80 on. It is nearly silent after a2 choices (prev_action=2: 0.4% rate) and after rare transitions (prev_common=0: 0.8%). The only future variable is action == 1, used for the window first trial, where the previous trial is outside the window. That is the agent own upcoming choice, a legitimate proxy for the unseen prev a1 choice. The core clause, prev a1 common, uses only observed history. Without the first-trial fallback, the observed-only predicate gets dev F1 0.75 (precision 0.80). With it, dev F1 0.82 and mass recall 0.95. False positives are mostly long a1-rewarded streaks where the activation has decayed to zero. In consecutive a1->S1 trials, magnitude visibly decays from one trial to the next (seen in the examples).

issues: Minor: the 'nearly silent after a2 (0.4%)' and 'after rare (0.8%)' rates are per step over all phases. Counting D1 steps only, the precision of (phase==D1)&(prev_action==2) is 0.015 on test and of (phase==D1)&(prev_common==0) is 0.029. The feature is still effectively silent there, but the quoted numbers flatter it about 3x.

The ep_trial<60 cutoff simplifies a gradual decline. Precision of the core clause by trial range on dev: trials <30 0.96, 30-60 0.67, 50-60 0.47, 60-70 0.26, 70-80 0.03. Nothing fires at trial 80 or later (test: 0 of 80136 D1 steps). Moving the cutoff barely changes dev F1 (50: 0.810, 55: 0.818, 60: 0.816, 65: 0.805).

Systematic but acknowledged false-positive class: repeated a1->S1 common trials. When the trial two back was also a1->S1 common, precision is 0.75. When the a1->S1 common trial follows a different trial type, precision is 0.96 (dev, trial <60). In misses --split test the main false-positive windows are long a1/S1c/rewarded streaks. Adding streak-break or reward terms to the predicate did not raise F1 (0.809 vs 0.816).

The reward claim holds: after a1->S1 common, precision is 0.778 after rewarded trials and 0.898 after unrewarded ones (test). The feature fires slightly more reliably after unrewarded trials, so 'not gated by reward' is accurate.

The fallback using the future variable action==1 only covers window-truncation cases (prev_action==-1). The observed-only core clause scores test F1 0.750 (precision 0.807), as stated. A good==1 fallback (hidden state) does worse on dev (precision 0.546 vs 0.605). The agent's upcoming choice is a fair proxy for the previous a1 choice it actually saw.

Verified: zero activation at GO and D2 (test: 0 of 791460 steps). prev_state==1 after a2 (rare) gives about 0 recall, and a1 with a rare transition to S2 gives 0, so the feature needs a1 AND reaching S1, not just S1. Test scores reproduce: P 0.755, R 0.89, F1 0.817, mass recall 0.95.
